whose reliability degrades under distribution shift because it silently over-applies inside-manifold priors. An explicit checklist functions as an externalized, frozen cognitive prosthesis: it enforces decomposition (breaking a holistic judgement into verifiable features), forces coverage of necessary criteria, and reduces omitted-variable error. When non-expert judgements on each item are near-independent (noise not correlated), the aggregate binary or scored output reduces variance by roughly 1/\u221an. The 'more reliable on average' claim thus holds only where (i) the checklist is causally complete for the outcome and (ii) within-item inter-rater correlation is below a threshold that would otherwise make aggregation futile. The evidence distinguishing a genuine gain from compliance-tracking is the pattern of errors on adversarial items whose surface features match the checklist but whose underlying outcome is inverted: genuine decomposition will catch these via cross-feature constraints, while rote checklist compliance will fail right alongside the surface cues.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
